summary: High-level discovery for porting from OpenAI/Anthropic and self-hosted vLLM/TGI to Redwood. Agreed next steps: pricing sheet, compatibility checklist, sample prompts for pilot, schedule bench run.

Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Liam: Liam here, CTO. Asha and Ravi and Marta are on.
[00:10] Asha: hi all, thanks.
[00:12] Jordan: Awesome. Priya from our infra team is with me — Priya, you wanna intro?
[00:16] Priya: Yep hey — Priya, SE, I own compatibility and perf on inference side.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to understand your stack, constraints, and what success looks like so we can propose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options.
[00:28] Liam: To be blunt we've been on OpenAI for chat generation and also running a small vLLM cluster for retrieval-augmented generation — we use TGI for some experiments. Cost is spiking and latency needs to tighten for product features.
[00:40] Marta: And quality — we ran side-by-side prompts vs OpenAI and saw minor drift on some edge cases. We need eval parity.
[00:48] Priya: When you say vLLM cluster, is that the open-source vLLM or a managed distro?
[00:52] Liam: It's self-hosted vLLM on GCP instances, public ingest, not air-gapped. We have a TGI container for some fine-tuning runs, but inference path is mainly vLLM.
[01:02] Priya: Got it. Two common paths — keep self-hosted but use Redwood Private to standardize, or migrate serving to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated. What are the drivers?
[01:12] Asha: Primary: predictable latency and ops overhead. Secondary: security/compliance needs — SOC2 is upcoming, and we need KMS integration, SSO, and audit logs.
[01:22] Ravi: Also data residency for some EU customers. We need VPC peering or a private hosting option.
[01:30] Jordan: Understood. For latency, can you give SLOs? p95 target?
[01:34] Liam: p95 about 150-200ms for short conversational turn responses (<= 256 tokens). Some longer responses acceptable up to 500ms.
[01:42] Priya: That's reasonable. For Hosted we can hit those with our optimized runtime and batching; Dedicated gives more predictable tail latencies because you own the pool. Private (VPC) brings more network variability but we provide tools to minimize it.
[01:56] Marta: What about model parity — if we were on OpenAI we rely on their latest models. Can Redwood host latest open models and preserve prompt behavior?
[02:04] Jordan: Short answer: yes, but there's nuance. We maintain a model catalog with vetted variants. For parity we run eval suites and tune quantization and tokenization to match outputs. Some prompts may need small prompt engineering changes.
[02:16] Asha: And for TGI/vLLM specifically — will Redwood accept checkpoints or do we need to re-run model conversion?
[02:22] Priya: We can ingest standard checkpoints, but sometimes runtime differences (quantization format, fused kernels) change outputs slightly. We keep a compatibility checklist — e g, safe to bring PT or GGUF, watch for 4-bit quantization artifacts — we'll share that.
[02:36] Liam: are there gotchas with KV cache or long context? Our app uses fairly long chat histories (2k–4k tokens).
[02:44] Priya: We manage KV cache across requests; losses are possible if sequence lengths exceed certain thresholds with some quantized kernels. For 4k you might need different execution paths; we recommend a profile run.
[02:54] Jordan: In previous migrations we've done small pilot benchmarks on customer prompts to validate latency and quality. Typically we run 1k representative queries and compare.
[03:02] Marta: That would be ideal. We'll share the sample prompts.
[03:06] Ravi: Security — SSO, SAML, SCIM provisioning, and KMS integration. Can Redwood support HSM-backed keys?
[03:14] Priya: Yes, we integrate with major KMS and HSM providers in Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports managed KMS with bring-your-own-key options for enterprise tiers. We also provide audit logs and key rotation policies.
[03:26] Asha: What about data retention — do you keep user inputs? We need policy to not persist sensitive PII and be able to purge.
[03:34] Jordan: By default Hosted retains logs for X days — enterprise can configure retention and purge. Dedicated/Private lets you control retention fully. We can add a sidecar redaction pipeline and token-level redaction rules.
[03:46] Liam: Sounds good. Cost — our CFO flagged per-token costs; can you ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:52] Jordan: I'll send a pricing sheet, but rough guidance: Hosted is lowest up-front but per-token slightly higher; Dedicated has a monthly commitment with lower marginal token cost; Private has infra and setup fees but is best for strict compliance. We'll model it for your current 100M tokens/month.
[04:10] Marta: On the quality/regression monitoring side — do you have hooks for our eval sets?
[04:16] Priya: Redwood Optimize ties monitoring to prompt sets, and can alert on regression. We also keep diffs and example fails.
[04:22] Liam: About vendor lock — we've heard concerns migrating back if needed. How reversible is this?
[04:28] Jordan: We design for portability: you can pin model versions, export checkpoints and logs, and we provide a migration playbook. For on-prem exact parity may need some re-tuning but we aim to minimize lock-in.
[04:40] Asha: Any known incompatibilities with TGI?
[04:44] Priya: TGI is mostly fine; certain custom ops in TGI fine-tunes sometimes, but we have community-tested adapters. We'll share examples.
[04:54] Liam: Can you summarize a pilot scope?
[04:58] Jordan: Sure — pilot: 1) ingest sample prompts (you), 2) Redwood spins up a dedicated test pool with your chosen model variant, 3) run 1k-5k queries, measure latency/cost, 4) run eval parity vs OpenAI baseline, 5) security review. Target 2–3 weeks for bench if all artifacts are ready.
[05:18] Marta: That timeline works if we can get people to respond quickly.
[05:22] Ravi: Onlegal/procurement — we'll need an NDA/MPA and SOC2 docs.
[05:26] Jordan: We'll send standard enterprise packet and SOC2 report.
[05:30] [00:06:00] Jordan: Quick question — you mentioned EU residency. Which regions do you need?
[05:34] Liam: Ireland and Germany mainly.
[05:38] Priya: We have EU-hosted infra options for Dedicated and Private; hosted may be possible depending on region availability.
[05:44] Asha: We also have a performance question: burst capacity during peak — 10x normal load for short windows. How does Redwood handle that?
[05:52] Jordan: Dedicated supports burst through autoscaling and reserved spare capacity; Hosted can handle bursts but depends on quota — we can provision higher tiers for predictable bursts. Private autoscaling depends on your infra.
[06:04] Marta: Any previous similar customers?
[06:06] Jordan: Yes, a couple of fintech and health teams moved off OpenAI to our Dedicated offering for cost reasons; we can share anonymized case study.
[06:12] Liam: OK. For the bench, do you need models checkpointed from us? We have finetuned variants.
[06:18] Priya: If you want exact parity we prefer provided checkpoints but we also can run open-model equivalents. If finetunes are small we can load them; we'll check format and tokenizers.
[06:28] Marta: One concern — prompt outputs sometimes contain hallucinations that are safe but need mitigation. Do you offer guardrails?
[06:34] Jordan: We have function-calling, structured outputs, and safety filters; also can run a reranker step to reduce unsafe outputs.
[06:42] Ravi: On the SOC2 note, our auditors will want to see encryption in transit and at rest, key rotation, and logging. Can you provide log retention and export?
[06:52] Priya: Yes for Dedicated/Private we give access to audit logs and S3 exports; Hosted has enterprise log exports.
[06:58] [00:12:00] Asha: Let's talk about the off-ramps — if we commit to Dedicated and then need to bring in-house, what's the effort?
[07:04] Jordan: We'll give a migration playbook and assist with export of models and data; complexity depends on custom infra and any proprietary kernels used. We try to avoid proprietary binary-only formats that block export.
[07:16] Liam: Score — cost, latency, compliance. Those are our KPIs. If you can show 20% lower cost for same latency, that's compelling.
[07:24] Jordan: We'll model that in the pricing sheet and run bench tests.
[07:28] Marta: Could you share a sample bench report and the metrics you capture?
[07:32] Priya: Yes — latency p50/p95, throughput, token cost, model divergence (BLEU/ROUGE or embedding distance), and sample failing prompts. We'll share a template.
[07:44] Liam: About vLLM — we've tuned for batching patterns and micro-batching. If Redwood uses different batching heuristics, could that change observed latency?
[07:52] Priya: Absolutely, batching strategy affects tail. We have continuous batching and can tune batch windows to mimic your behavior. We'll need your real request traces.
[07:62] [note: timestamp drift] Marta: ha, these timestamps are off a bit.
[08:00] Asha: procurement timeline — we hope to decide by end of Q1 2027. Is that feasible?
[08:06] Jordan: Yes. Pilot in Jan, decision in Feb/March is feasible.
[08:10] Ravi: Any blockers on our side for pilot?
[08:12] Priya: Mostly sample prompts, a small credentialed account for test traffic, and confirmation on which model variant you want to test.
[08:20] Liam: We'll prepare those.
[08:22] Jordan: Great. We'll send an email with links: pricing sheet, SOC2, technical checklist, and a short onboarding doc.
[08:28] Marta: Please include the vLLM/TGI gotchas.
[08:30] Priya: Will do.
[08:32] [00:30:00] Jordan: Any final questions?
[08:34] Liam: Not right now. Thanks for the time.
[08:36] Asha: Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Jordan: Recap — Jordan to send pricing and packet, Priya to send compatibility checklist and bench template, Sundial to share prompts and KMS/SSO details. We'll aim to schedule bench 2027-01-11 week.
[08:50] [00:45:00] Jordan: I'll follow up with calendar invites and the enterprise packet. Thanks all.
[08:55] Marta: thanks. bye.
[08:58] [End of recording]
